units.translation: and in the reins he held a mouth well-fitted to the bit
when the ear of young summer is parched
thus Stanley for ἡνιοστρόφου [of the rein-turner]
I guide the reins beyond the course
It is the seat of the emotions:
and he will devour the liver, blackened with gore
many things, at any rate, touch the liver
no sting of grief reaches the liver
uttering hot words of ruin from the liver
grieve the liver with just reproaches
they hold the whole mainland-born race
where I wrote ἠπείροιν [of the two mainlands] with Herwerden, Exerc. crit. p. 93.
you will come to the Asian mainland
when you cross the stream that is the boundary of the mainlands
having emptied the whole expanse of the mainland
to have been saved to this mainland
ἠπίοις [gentle] is a corruption for νηπίοις [childish], which see.
to sound, to utter a sound
I sound, I utter a sound

Thus Lachmann for ἀΰπνων — διὰ στόμα [sleepless — through the mouth]. On the three other passages see under ἀπύω. The Doric form ἀπύω [I sound] is frequent in the tragedians, on which see Thes. vol. 1, 2 p. 1842.
and they sounded the horse-guiding mouthpieces of the fire-thundering bridles
neither a sign of winter nor of flowery spring
in the appearing spring it shakes its wing
with the second eta changed to alpha, the verse being defective, which I restored thus: ὦ πότνι᾽ ἴθι Διὸς παραγενοῦ δάμαρ [O lady, come, be present, wife of Zeus], deleting the gloss Ἥρα [Hera].
subdued by the wrathful counsels of Hera
what sufferings must be endured at the hands of Hera
by the wandering wanderings of Hera
the pledges of Hera Teleia and Zeus
the key-holding priestess of Hera – Io
and these are the hidden torments of Hera
with the goad-driven pains of Hera
for she is able, being nearest to Zeus, with Hera
Hera Teleia, the wedded wife of Zeus
libations first to Zeus of the ripe marriage and to Hera
O lady, come, be present, wife of Zeus
was the title of a play of Aeschylus (fr. 69-71).
Hesychius s.v. and in Aeschylus (fr. 357) the lioness early-born, either she who gives birth in the air, or she who gives birth in spring.
the lioness early-born, either she who gives birth in the air, or she who gives birth in spring
and the heroes who sent them
the second libation I assign to the heroes
Hesione, daughter of Oceanus, wife of Prometheus
when you brought Hesione, your father's sister
we are in the power of the stronger, as if defeated
for it is not fitting for the lesser to speak boldly
for everyone bears goodwill to the lesser
rejoicing no less than in the Zeus-given delight of the sown seed
you tell me these things no less worthy of tears
nor would you be less a friend to the house
with quiet step of the mind
but her acting openly, more quiet
